L2_data_source_availability.detail: Inputs/ST2/Inputs/ExternalSources/Mohun/ shared with Ch14 covers Mohun's BLS CES + NIPA construction. Specific files used: mohun_unproductive_decomposition_1948_1989.csv, mohun_unproductive_decomposition_by_industry.csv, mohun_employment_by_industry_1948_1989.csv, mohun_industry_classification.csv. BLS CES + NIPA upstream APIs are public.
gaps: Coverage in CSVs is 1948-1989 (Mohun 2005 era); Mohun 2013 extends to 2010. Years 1990-2010 require either separate digitization from the 2013 paper Tables 2-3, or BLS CES API extension. Currently registry status=book_period_validated indicates the extension to 2010 is not yet executed.

L3_methodology_clarity.detail: All four research JSONs populated with verbatim_quote schema. ES1501: working class unproductive labor (Lu_wc) via CES production-worker criterion; key empirical finding documented (12.8% money-value-added absorption flat 1964-2010, contradicting Moseley/Paitaridis-Tsoulfidis burden thesis). ES1502/ES1503/ES1504 cover related decompositions. Construction formulas explicit (ES1501-COMBINED = Mohun Lu * 0.813).
gaps: ES1501-A construction note documents the 0.813 working-class share factor — this is a derived approximation from Mohun's stable class proportions; should be flagged as a composite construction in V03.

L5_validation_refs.detail: validation.reference_values present in registry but sparse. Research JSONs contain rich benchmark text (unprod working class employment share 25.1% 1964 -> 30.0% 2007; wage share 18.6% 1964 -> 16.7% 1992 -> 18.1% 2010; money-value-added absorption 12.9% 1964 = 12.9% 2010). Many of these published series-level benchmarks have not been pulled into validation.reference_values yet.
gaps: Pull Mohun Fig 2/Fig 4 benchmark values into validation.reference_values for ES1501-ES1504 — currently relies on a single reference point per series.

L6_classification_accuracy.detail: content_type=time_series correct (annual 1964-2010 panel). No proxy flag needed for direct Mohun digitizations. ES1501's '0.813 working class share' multiplier is documented as a stable empirical share (sd 0.88pp across 1964-2010), which is faithful to Mohun's reported class composition — not a proxy.
gaps: The 0.813 multiplier is a constant — flag in registry as construction.notes='constant_share_approximation' for transparency. Not strictly a proxy, but a documented simplification.
